briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax-Relief Momentum Builds in Lansing as Psilocybin and M&A Fuel National Cannabis Surge
briefs.top: Michigan senators and a leading governor candidate are now both pushing to roll back the state's 24% wholesale cannabis tax, while operators show real resilience with steady demand and a new Ypsilanti storefront opening. Nationally, Compass Pathways' psilocybin treatment is racing toward a Q4 FDA filing, Curaleaf is pressing a hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis, and DEA's rescheduling pause leaves the existing medical Schedule III order untouched.

local.text: Eight state senators now push to repeal 24% tax — Sen. Jonathan Lindsey, who sponsors S.B. 810, called the 24% wholesale tax nonessential to Michigan's pocketbook to the detriment of the state's cannabis industry, and at least one senator who voted in the majority to pass the act last year has changed her mind since.

GOP governor hopeful courts industry with tax-cut vow — GOP gubernatorial candidate John James says the cannabis tax 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections,' and pledged 'As Governor, I will work to repeal or sharply reduce it', and the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association has officially endorsed James, citing his commitment to repealing the levy.

Demand holds steady despite the new wholesale tax — while overtaxed markets often see demand suffer, that doesn't seem to be the case so far in 2026, indicating licensed businesses are absorbing the 24% tax in an oversupplied marketplace with 956 cultivation licensees, 275 processors and 835 dispensaries.
Bloom City Club opens new Ypsilanti storefront — the Ann Arbor-rooted retailer is celebrating the new Ypsilanti store with several cannabis-themed events in October.

State purges bad actors, clearing field for clean brands — regulators revoked 20 cultivation licenses and fined a company $2 million after it shipped packages labeled as marijuana that actually contained 'dirt and mulch', while Muha Meds lost its Ypsilanti dispensary license and was fined more than $250,000 for using a fake customer profile to illegally sell product.

national.text: DEA pause doesn't touch the medical Schedule III order — a DEA judge paused the broader cannabis rescheduling proceeding while weighing a new GAO report, adding another procedural step for operators awaiting a decision on whether adult-use joins medical cannabis on Schedule III, but the stay leaves in place the April 2026 order covering FDA-approved marijuana products and state-licensed medical marijuana.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin stays on track for Q4 filing — Compass Pathways expects to complete its New Drug Application for COMP360 psilocybin treatment in Q4 2026, with commercial launch anticipated in the first half of 2027, which would make it the first classic psychedelic ever approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Curaleaf raises hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis — Curaleaf raised its unsolicited offer for Aurora Cannabis to $5 per share, pushing for a fair process and arguing shareholders deserve the same diligence access offered to other potential acquirers.

Spherex goes vertical with Colorado cultivation buy — Colorado's leading cannabis brand agreed to acquire two cultivation facilities from The Cannabist Company in its first-ever acquisition, with roughly 60 employees joining and growing the company to nearly 100 workers.

New York cannabis sales blow past $4 billion — New York's recreational marijuana dispensaries have now sold more than $4 billion worth of legal cannabis products, state officials announced, a marker of how fast mature adult-use markets can scale.
